title: Who Can Sudo
scenario: A support analyst was granted broad sudo access during an incident. AI says the account is low risk because it is not an administrator account.
objective: Reduce sudo authority to the minimum command needed for log review and document why account labels do not establish privilege.
ai_native_dimension: AI provides an incomplete privilege assessment based on username/account role rather than effective sudo rights.

verification.message: broad passwordless sudo must be removed

aar_questions: What was the security problem in Who Can Sudo and what objective evidence proved it?
What was the risk if it remained unresolved?
What did you change and why?
How did you verify the result independently of AI output?
Where did AI help, where was it wrong/incomplete, and what remained your responsibility?
seeded_ai_response: Because the account is named analyst rather than admin, privilege escalation is unlikely.
